name: Bold
label: Revelation
lede: A Westchester band too young for the CBGB door cut one album in Youth of Today's studio, borrowed its look from Run-D.M.C. and Van Halen, and watched the record outlive the band by decades.

eras.title: Standing outside CBGB
eras.text: Katonah sits forty miles up the commuter line, and Matt Warnke was 13 or 14 when record shops, fanzines and friends' older siblings pulled him into hardcore. He and his John Jay High School friends were on the CBGB matinee stage before most of them could legally get in.

yt: Warnke on Crippled Youth and Bold, NYHC Chronicles
years.h: Crippled Youth start up in Katonah, forty miles from CBGB
years.p: Matt Warnke sings and plays guitar, [[Tim Brooks|f8e01057-29f6-4be5-968e-4220d6a48ff3]] plays bass, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] drums. Warnke is under 16, so his first trips to CBGB mean standing outside.
years.xp:
The record that hit Warnke hardest was [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s Victim in Pain.

The commuter train from Katonah got the kids to midtown Manhattan in 45 minutes, which is how a group of high schoolers ended up in the front rows of the city's hardcore matinees.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Search: 1985–1989 · Tony Rettman, No Idols
years.h: Join the Fight, Crippled Youth's debut 7", on New Beginning
years.p: Crippled Youth recorded it in December 1985. Mike Trouchon's California label, New Beginning, put it out in 1986.
years.xp: The record got a feature in Maximum Rock'N'Roll. The first sleeves went out with the layout ruler accidentally left in under the back-cover photo. It's the earliest material Revelation later gathered on The Search.

years.h: First CBGB matinee, on a bill with Warzone and Youth of Today
years.p: [[Rest In Pieces|3cb8bd68-6c42-4dea-b0c6-f33c66cc790b]] play too. John Zuluaga, known as Zulu, joins on guitar and Matt Warnke moves to vocals only.
years.xp:
Warnke had been going to CBGB since 1985, but under 16 that mostly meant hanging around outside. In June 1986 he got in the door and onto the stage, and was surprised how many people were up front: "singing the words."

That year's other jolt was the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] demo, which Warnke remembers as a cultural shift. Bands on the bill that day: [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] and [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]].

eras.title: Reach Out becomes Speak Out
eras.text: By the time the album came around the band had dropped the name Crippled Youth for Bold, and a California label was lined up to release it. Then Jordan Cooper wrote out his case for Revelation, and it became REV 9.

years.src: No Echo: Matt Warnke and John Zuluaga · RevHQ: Bold, Speak Out
yt: Bold at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, July 17, 1988
years.h: Jordan Cooper's term paper gets Speak Out to Revelation
years.p: The album was meant for Wishing Well Records in Orange County. Cooper talked the band out of it, and it came out as Revelation REV 9.
years.xp:
John Zuluaga remembers Warnke handing him what looked like a term paper from Cooper, laying out why Speak Out belonged on Revelation. Cooper then had to collect the master reels from Wishing Well, whose Pat Longrie took it well. The working title was Reach Out.

Bold recorded at Electric Reels with Dan Nichols producing, the studio where Youth of Today had cut Break Down the Walls. The look came from outside hardcore: Warnke pointed to Run-D.M.C.'s Raising Hell and Stetsasonic's On Fire for the tinted photos and block logo, and Van Halen's first album for the quadrant layout.

About ten years later Speak Out got a second life, as a straight edge revival in Ohio spread outward and new kids went looking for the originals.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

eras.title: Pink vinyl, then everybody scatters
eras.text: Tom Capone joined on second guitar and Bold got heavier and more careful. They cut a 7" and a second record in 1989, then scattered into the bands that pushed New York hardcore somewhere new.

years.p: Three songs on Revelation REV 11, and the first record with [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] on second guitar.
years.xp: The colored vinyl was supposed to be maroon to match the sleeve, but the plant couldn't mix it right.

years.h: Drew Thomas starts Into Another, Tom Capone heads for Quicksand
years.p: Thomas helps start [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] in 1990. Capone goes on to [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], and later Handsome and Instruction.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Bold's run to 1993, but no later shows or records are documented.

years.h: Two years after the last session, Looking Back
years.p: Bold finished their final recordings by February 1989. Revelation put them out in 1991.
years.xp: Revelation later reissued Looking Back as a 12" with two bonus tracks.

eras.title: The Bold that wasn't
eras.text: Matt Warnke got back on stage with a new band that played some old Bold songs and had no name of its own. A Connecticut flyer billed them as Bold, and not everyone was happy about it.

years.big: "This isn't BOLD, but we're going to do some of those songs."
q: The most authentic reaction I'd ever seen at a show.
years.src: No Echo: The story behind the fake Bold reunion
years.h: A Connecticut flyer bills Warnke's new band as Bold
years.p: Matt Warnke, to the crowd at the New Milford Teen Center after the first song. With Eddie McNamara, Chris Daley and Matt Martin he'd already played the Wetlands and CBGB, but the flyer had people expecting a reunion.
years.xp:
The band had no settled name and was mixing Bold songs into a new, post-hardcore set. They had planned to play originals, and dropped the idea once the billing spread. McNamara later said he "felt like a poseur."

The crowd didn't mind: fans rushed the stage and sang along, and someone broke part of the ceiling. The band carried on as Endure, then One Sided War. The real reunion, with the Speak Out core, was nine years off.

eras.title: A reunion, for real this time
eras.text: Revelation's retrospective got Bold back together, with an old friend from Youth of Today and Judge on second guitar. By the label's 25th birthday they were a fixture of its anniversary bills on both coasts.

years.p: Sixty-six minutes: Looking Back, Speak Out, compilation tracks, two unreleased songs and the Crippled Youth 7", from the last session back to the first.

years.h: Warnke, Capone and Brooks get Bold back together
years.p: Vinny Panza plays drums, and [[John Porcelly|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] sits in on second guitar.

years.h: Warnke and Porcelly step away, and Bold are done again
years.p: The singer and the guest guitarist leave, which Wikipedia says effectively ends the reunion.

years.cap: Bold at the Glass House, Pomona, June 9, 2012
yt: Bold at a Revelation 25 show, fan-shot
years.h: Bold play the Glass House for Revelation's 25th birthday
years.p: The West Coast leg of the label's anniversary shows, 24 years after Speak Out came out on it.

years.cap: Bold at Irving Plaza, New York, October 13, 2012
years.h: Irving Plaza, in the city whose matinees they grew up in
years.p: The New York leg of Revelation's 25th anniversary, 26 years after Crippled Youth's first CBGB matinee.

eras.title: Thirty-five and embossed
eras.text: Revelation gave Speak Out the full 35th-anniversary treatment, and Bold kept playing to people who weren't born when it came out.

years.big: "At the time, I was definitely not thinking about longevity."
years.src: No Echo: Matt Warnke and John Zuluaga
years.h: Speak Out turns 35 in an embossed gatefold
years.p: John Zuluaga on the album's staying power. Revelation's remaster has a 40-page booklet designed by John Scharbach, plus color variants and a cassette.
years.xp: The gatefold layout was Drew Thomas's idea, inspired by KISS album covers. The reissue arrived after a straight edge revival in several countries sent new listeners to the original.

years.h: John Porcelly is back on second guitar for Bold in California
years.p: Bold play a run of California shows with [[John Porcelly|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] in the spot again.

years.h: Bold and Youth of Today hit the Northeast 39 years after CBGB
years.p: The Meadows in Brooklyn, the Lithuanian Music Hall in Philadelphia and Amityville Music Hall, with Swedish Revelation band Speedway opening. The two bands had shared a CBGB bill in June 1986.

years.h: Bold open for Orange 9mm in Orlando
years.p: The ticket is $30, at Conduit, with Bold opening for the reunited New York post-hardcore band.
